title: Derived maps out of a perfect constant complex are locally algebraic
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with final object $X$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $R$ be a commutative ring. Use constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $P,L\in D(R)$ with $P$ perfect, meaning that it is represented by a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. For every morphism $\varphi:\underline P\to\underline L$ in $D(\mathcal C,\underline R)$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to X\}$ and morphisms $\alpha_i:P\to L$ in $D(R)$ such that $\varphi|_{U_i}=\underline{\alpha_i}|_{U_i}$ in $D(\mathcal C/U_i,\underline R|_{U_i})$. Here restriction and the localized site are [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. No boundedness or finiteness is required of $L$, and the site need not have points.

source.place: Tag 09BE, lemma-locally-constant-map; exact statement, for a commutative coefficient ring.

proof.text: Choose a bounded finite-projective complex $F^\bullet$ and an isomorphism $QF^\bullet\simeq P$ by perfectness, and choose any complex $G^\bullet$ with $QG^\bullet\simeq L$. Constant presheaves preserve exact sequences because their values and maps are the original sequence at every object. Module-valued sheafification is exact, so constant realization is exact. The module-sheafification interface identifies its underlying abelian sheaves and its $\underline R$-action with the constant module sheaves in the statement. Exact-functor derived factorization therefore gives canonical representative isomorphisms $Q(\underline F^\bullet)\simeq\underline P$ and $Q(\underline G^\bullet)\simeq\underline L$. Replace $\varphi$ using these isomorphisms. This requires no boundedness of $G^\bullet$ and no Noetherian hypothesis on $R$.

source.place: Tag 09BE, lemma-locally-constant-map, choice of representatives; exact constant realization as in the preceding paragraph, with Sites Tag 00WJ

proof.text: Apply the local-chain-representative lemma to $F^\bullet$ and the arbitrary sheaf complex $\underline G^\bullet$. It supplies a covering on which the replaced morphism is represented by a chain map $a:\underline F^\bullet\to\underline G^\bullet$. Work on each such slice, whose final object is the covering object. The hypothesis on the source is precisely boundedness with finitely generated projective terms; the target need not be perfect or bounded.

source.place: Tag 09BE, first cited input Tag 09BD, lemma-map-out-of-locally-constant

proof.text: There are only finitely many possibly nonzero components $a^q$, since $F^\bullet$ is bounded. By the constant-restriction lemma, the restrictions of $\underline{F^q}$ and $\underline{G^q}$ to the slice are the constant module sheaves of the slice site, compatibly with the constant-presheaf units and with restriction of constant linear maps. Apply the site constant-morphism-local lemma on the slice to each $a^q:\underline{F^q}\to\underline{G^q}$: $F^q$ is finitely generated. In each covering sieve choose an actual covering family contained in it. Successively refine these covers, using the covering-pullback and transitivity axioms. This is a finite iteration, so gives a covering on which, for each nondegenerate covering object $V$ (one not covered by the empty sieve), all components have algebraic representatives $b_V^q:F^q\to G^q$ simultaneously. On a degenerate object $V$, every further object over $V$ is also covered by the empty sieve, so every module sheaf restricts to zero by the unique-gluing axiom; take all $b_V^q=0$. Degrees with $F^q=0$ are also assigned zero. No arbitrary fibre products beyond covering pullbacks and no points of the topos are used; each covering sieve is realized by a covering family contained in it.

source.place: Tag 09BE, second cited input Modules on Sites Tag 093S(3), lemma-morphism-locally-constant; finite common refinement

proof.text: For a nondegenerate $V$ and any $R$-module $T$, the constant-section unit $T\to\underline T(V)$ is injective. Indeed the module-sheafification interface and the underlying-set sheafification lemma identify this unit with set sheafification of the constant presheaf. If $t$ and $t'$ have the same image, the sheafification-sections-local lemma supplies a covering of $V$ on which they agree as presheaf sections. That covering cannot be empty, because $V$ is nondegenerate; all restrictions of the constant presheaf are identities, hence $t=t'$. Apply this to $T=G^{q+1}$ and the values on every $x\in F^q$ of $d_G^q b_V^q$ and $b_V^{q+1}d_F^q$. Their constant sections agree because $a$ is a chain map and its components are the constant realizations of the $b_V^q$. Injectivity proves $d_G^q b_V^q=b_V^{q+1}d_F^q$ algebraically in every degree, including the two boundary degrees of the support of $F$. On degenerate $V$ these equations hold because all $b_V^q=0$. Thus $b_V^\bullet:F^\bullet\to G^\bullet$ is a chain map. Define $\alpha_V:P\to L$ by $P\simeq QF^\bullet\xrightarrow{Q(b_V)}QG^\bullet\simeq L$. The naturality of the exact-functor representative isomorphisms identifies its constant realization with $Q(a)$ on $V$, hence with $\varphi|_V$. Transitivity of the two successive covering constructions gives the required covering of $X$.
